headline: Foggy mornings and sunny afternoons through Thursday; weak front brings brief light rain and cooler air Friday.
summary: High pressure keeps western Washington quiet and mostly dry through Thursday, with foggy mornings and sunny afternoons in the upper 60s. A weak front arrives late Friday into Saturday, bringing only a few hundredths of an inch of rain that won't last long. The bigger change is cooler air: Friday highs drop to the low 60s, with breezy winds along the coast and Puget Sound waterfronts, and snow levels fall to around 5000 feet, so the North Cascades may get a dusting. The weekend turns colder, with frost or freeze possible for farms and sensitive plants, though that is still being watched. Another chance of rain Tuesday into Wednesday is uncertain because computer models disagree on the low's position.
changes: The Dense Fog Advisory for the inland waters ran only until noon, and later discussions shifted the front's arrival from Friday to late Friday into Saturday. The evening update also said overnight fog is most likely from Bellingham to Everett.
